newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey starts partial pullout from northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey starts partial pullout from northern Iraq.

text.p: Turkey has begun a partial withdrawal of its forces from northern Iraq were they have been fighting Kurdish rebels for the past five weeks, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Thursday.
It said that more than 50 tanks and armoured vehicles had returned to Turkey over the last week but added that some operations were continuing near the border.

Much of the Arab world and some of Turkey's Western allies had condemned Ankara for the cross-border drive against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the mountainous area for attacks into Turkish territory.
Turkey says it has killed many more than 1,000 guerrillas but Western diplomats say that figure is inflated.
An Iraqi Kurdish militia group had joined Turkish troops in the recent operation.
More that 24,000 people have been killed in Turkey's 12-year conflict with the PKK, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in Turkey.
